rationale: island seed
island seed

A short 3-day pullback in a high-margin, pricing-power-rich business is more likely a liquidity-driven overreaction worth buying, whereas the same dip in a structurally weak-margin business more likely reflects genuine deterioration, so margin rank rescales how hard to fade it.
Volume many standard deviations above its own recent norm marks a surge in urgent or informed participation that same-day price only partially absorbs, leaving a drift to complete.
A wide intraday trading range relative to the day's starting price is a direct footprint of thin order-book depth, so persistently range-heavy names carry a standing liquidity-risk premium.

Earnings propped up by large accruals are most likely to be actively repriced exactly when a stock sees abnormally elevated trading relative to its own recent history, i.e. informed flow confirming the accrual mispricing is resolving now.

Operating margin times asset turnover reconstructs DuPont operating ROA independent of financing choices; subtracting a separate leverage rank isolates firms generating returns through operating efficiency rather than balance-sheet risk-taking.

Under-reaction to news diffuses more slowly in names with structurally wider trading ranges (higher information uncertainty), so a recency-weighted trend should predict better precisely where realised range-volatility is elevated, a cross-sectional interaction distinct from scaling a return by its own time-series volatility.

A persistent tilt in the overnight open-versus-prior-close ratio reflects informed order flow that arrives after the close, a channel that predicts next-session continuation separately from ordinary close-to-close momentum, which is dominated by intraday noise trading.

Where today's price-normalized range sits within a stock's own six-month distribution captures a relative illiquidity-regime extreme that a smoothed level ratio dilutes, and trading-friction extremes resolve slowly as depth is rebuilt.

Rule 2 already validated ABS(return)-vs-volume correlation over the signed form, so that structure stays untouched. The only remaining lever is horizon, and at 10 days this is on the short side relative to rule 3's slow/medium preference, so it is lengthened to 21.

This factor already matches rule 8's one validated fusion template (CS_RANK x TS_RANK), so that structure stays fixed. Its weak side is that the volume branch is exactly TS_RANK($dollar_volume,21), the raw-level pattern rule 4 names as saturating/correlation-rejected; ranking the 21-day change instead of the level fixes that side while preserving the symmetric normalization.

Same parent pair as pair 5, fused differently on purpose: A's quality product is divided directly by leverage (efficiency per unit of balance-sheet risk, one ratio instead of a separate subtracted rank) and ranked, then multiplied by B's raw, unsmoothed intraday range as an attention/repricing amplifier rather than a noise normalizer. Where pair 5 treats range as noise to divide out, this treats range as evidence that a leverage-light, efficient name is being actively repriced -- an opposite-in-spirit but equally legitimate fusion of the same two ideas.

Margin expansion is credible, sustainable operating leverage rather than an unsustainable price hike only when the firm already turns its assets over efficiently, so scaling margin improvement by turnover efficiency isolates the durable component of quality gains.
Trailing earnings per dollar of current price is a direct cheapness signal that predicts a return premium as the market's growth-expectation errors correct toward realized earnings power.

Asset turnover earned per unit of financial leverage isolates operating efficiency achieved organically rather than through debt-funded asset growth, a clean-quality combination the market prices more slowly than either metric alone.

Same over-mined range/dollar_volume family as rule 6 describes; window and denominator are already known dead ends. Switching the numerator from full range (high-low) to lower-wick (close-low) targets a support-recovery signal instead of raw range, and stays distinct from the other range-family mutation in this batch.

A range skewed toward the day's high versus its low, independent of the day's net move, shows which side of the order book absorbed more flow intraday, an imbalance that predicts short-term continuation or fade on the thinner side.

The accrual anomaly is strongest where mispricing is hardest to arbitrage; pairing weak earnings quality with a persistently wide intraday range isolates the high-uncertainty names where that mispricing survives longest.

A anchors position to a 21-day high/low channel; B averages range per dollar of volume traded (a liquidity-cost level). Keeps A's TS_MAX($high,21) ceiling (3 nodes) and B's ($high-$low) payload (3 nodes), but reproduces neither parent's own guarded denominator (A's TS_MAX-minus-TS_MIN channel width is 7 nodes; B's TS_MEAN-of-ratio over dollar_volume is 9), so no 4+ node piece repeats. The fusion is a normaliser swap: today's range is expressed against the stock's own recent price ceiling instead of against its liquidity level -- is the range large relative to where the stock has been trading, a price-scaled volatility question neither parent poses alone (A never measures range; B never references the channel high).

A averages a liquidity-scaled closing-strength ratio, (close-low)/dollar_volume; B ranks accrual-quality times a ranked 21-day dollar-volume change. Keeps B's TS_DELTA($dollar_volume,21) (3 nodes, wrapped in CS_RANK rather than B's own TS_RANK(...,21), so B's 5-node piece is not reproduced) and A's dollar-volume epsilon guard (3 nodes), reattached to a fresh numerator -- open-to-low, distinct from A's own close-to-low. The fusion is volume confirmation of intraday price action: a pullback-from-open scaled by today's liquidity is weighted by whether trading activity is genuinely picking up, a combination neither parent forms alone (A never looks at volume trend; B never looks at intraday structure).

Raw $return legs are flagged as fragile, and single-day ABS(return) is a noisy partner for volume. Replaced it with a short realized-vol measure, keeping the vol-volume relation but smoothing the signal.
Stacking two identical 21-day windows back to back on the volume leg is redundant and mostly overlapping. Shortened the inner delta to 5 days so the delta and rank horizons are distinct.

Today's range expansion relative to its 21-day norm, divided by the stock's own dollar-volume variability, isolates breakouts against a calm liquidity backdrop -- the signals most likely to reflect real information rather than noise from an already-erratic trading regime.

Smoothing or renormalizing $dollar_volume directly in this denominator shape is already known to stay correlated (rho 0.92+) with the archived version. Switching to TS_RANK($dollar_volume,5), an ordinal rather than level-based liquidity measure, strips out the cross-sectional level information that was driving that correlation.

TS_SUM($return,63) is exactly the same-asset $return-sum pattern flagged as this round's dominant failure mode and the thing cross-field/no-return kernels should replace. Swapped it for a 63-day liquidity-trend term, keeping the window and the untouched EPS leg.

A bare rank of one fundamental has no price or volume interaction, the exact gap fundamentals need this round. Multiplying by RANK($dollar_volume) keeps both legs as dimensionless cross-sectional ranks (unlike multiplying by a raw, unbounded level, which would just collapse to a liquidity-level sort).

21 days is long enough for a raw-$volume correlation to pick up secular drift in trading activity rather than genuine day-to-day co-movement with |return|. Shortening to 5 days keeps the same volatility-volume hypothesis but moves it to a faster, less trend-contaminated horizon.

The delta window and the outer TS_RANK window were both 21, so the factor compared a quantity to a same-length history of itself with no distinct timescale. Widening the inner delta to 63 days (a quarterly liquidity shift) while keeping the 21-day rank window asks whether this quarter's shift is extreme relative to the past month instead.

Under the mixture-of-distributions hypothesis, volume and intraday range are jointly driven by the rate of information arrival; strengthening co-movement flags informed-trading intensity ahead of continued directional moves.
Today's range relative to its own rolling ceiling flags climactic, liquidity-shock trading days; such extremes tend to mean-revert as liquidity providers step back in and re-tighten spreads.

The share of a month's dollar volume concentrated in its single busiest day measures how event-driven versus steady a stock's liquidity is; lumpy, spike-dominated volume signals unresolved information still diffusing into price.

Any outer-wrapper change to a bare single-field rank is a monotonic transform of the same variable (guaranteed rho 1), and TS-wraps/deltas on fundamentals already fail coverage or saturate. Swapped to a different reliable-coverage fundamental untried in this bare form.
Return-volume TS_CORR fails cheap_screen under every raw/SIGN/ABS transform tried (rule 6), which explicitly suggests ranking one leg first. Ranked the volume leg before correlating.

A's liquidity-normalized recovery-off-the-low idea and B's earnings-yield idea both anchor on $close, so the fusion swaps A's dollar_volume guard for B's own guarded-close (3 nodes from B) under A's close-low numerator (3 nodes from A), producing a fresh price-relative recovery ratio, then spreads it against a bare earnings-per-share rank. This asks whether a stock's valuation rank diverges from its own recovery-off-the-low rank: cheap-but-not-recovering vs cheap-and-recovering, an interaction neither single rank states. The shared RANK($earnings_per_share) leg already co-exists with two other admitted spreads on different second legs (618d10279664fdd6, d81c79a5c4e69097), which is empirical precedent that this leg alone does not push correlation past 0.80.

A's accrual-quality rank is spread against a new interaction term built from A's own volume-flow-delta (3 nodes) multiplied by B's range piece (3 nodes, ranked over a fresh 10-day window so it doesn't collide with the already-admitted TS_RANK(($high-$low),21) sibling ea4fceb6041540b0). The spread asks whether accrual quality diverges from a combined volume-acceleration/volatility-attention signal, a quality-vs-attention divergence that neither parent states: A multiplies quality by flow with no volatility term, B has no fundamental at all.

Both parents are pure price/volume with no fundamental leg, so the genuine fusion here is cross-domain rather than cross-asset-class: A's own-history range regime (63d, price side) times a cross-sectional rank of B's volume-instability level (TS_STD($volume,21), 3 nodes, B's only legal donation used unguarded to avoid recreating B's own guarded TS_STD($volume,21)+1e-8 denominator). This flags stocks simultaneously in an elevated own-history range regime and unusually erratic (relative to peers) trading volume, a compounding price-and-volume-stress interaction that neither parent states alone: A never touches volume, and B's own normalization is purely time-series/self-relative with no cross-sectional comparison.

Margin expansion that outpaces asset-turnover gains signals pricing-power-led profitability improvement rather than volume-chasing growth, a higher-quality source of gains the market re-rates as later quarters confirm it.

Earnings scaled by book capital times leverage measures profit generated per dollar of total capital employed, equity plus the debt layered on it, so it screens out firms whose per-share earnings look strong only because leverage inflated them.

Book value that grows alongside high current accruals is more likely accounting-driven than cash-driven, so equity growth paired with poor accrual quality should predict weaker forward returns than growth backed by low accruals.

Operational efficiency conditions how a short-term price swing should be read: in efficient, high-turnover businesses a recent move is more likely noise to fade, so gating recent return by asset-turnover rank should sharpen a reversal signal that plain return misses.

TS_SUM($return,63) is the same return-sum pattern id49's own lesson flagged as this run's dominant failure mode (rule 11); id49 already fixed it via a dollar-volume delta from this same parent, so this swaps the flagged leg for a plain liquidity-level rank instead, a distinct fix to the same weak component.

Captures whether medium-term momentum is accelerating or decelerating relative to the longer-term trend, expressed in units of the stock's own long-run volatility so the acceleration reading is comparable across risk levels.

Isolates earnings-power-supported price action from noise: a sudden short-horizon spike in raw share volume with no earnings-quality backing looks like speculative churn likely to fade, while the same spike in a high-earnings name looks like real information arrival.

A trading-range expansion that occurs in the same direction as the prevailing medium-term trend reflects broad participation and should continue, whereas the same range expansion against the trend is more likely noise.

RANK and CS_RANK are literal aliases here, and smoothing the $close denominator already failed twice this round (duplicate at TS_MEAN w=5, rho 0.998 at w=21), so any monotonic change to price or to the outer rank cannot decorrelate. Taking the magnitude of EPS is the one available non-monotonic lever: it reorders loss-making names relative to the signed-yield ranking while leaving the majority (profitable) names' order untouched.

Raw $dollar_volume is a dominant archived level (TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,21) is its own archive member; light wrappers around raw/smoothed dollar_volume hit rho 0.968-0.997 this run), so the liquidity normalizer itself is the weak part. Swapping to the stock's own 21-day close volatility keeps the same close-low numerator but scales it by price dispersion instead of any volume transform, avoiding both the raw-volume trap and duplicating af43733e3a6a1dbf's TS_RANK(volume) fix.

The second leg is an 8-node block on its own, so swapping the other (2-node) fundamental leg instead would leave it byte-identical and fail archive_subtree regardless of which fundamental is chosen. Replacing the intraday-range numerator with a 3-day price change keeps the same eps-guarded close-scaling but trades range-positioning for short momentum; every same-family OHLC-anchor swap tried elsewhere this run (open/high/low substitutions) stayed at rho >= 0.85, so the core comparison needed to change, not just which anchor is used.

A donates TS_RANK($dollar_volume, 5) (3 nodes) rather than its other legal piece ($close - $low): $close is dividend-adjusted and $low is raw, so subtracting them imports a scale artifact, and A's high fitness already looks suspicious for exactly this reason. B donates TS_RANK($dollar_volume, 63) (3 nodes, the only piece above CS_RANK($roe)'s 2). Fusion: the ratio of a short- and long-window liquidity percentile is a liquidity-regime-shift term, is today's relative trading activity elevated versus the stock's own quarterly norm, gated by quality. Neither parent states this: A never sees a 63-day liquidity window, B never sees a 5-day one, and a single-window rank cannot express acceleration in relative liquidity.

A donates TS_MAX($dollar_volume, 21) (3 nodes, the peak-liquidity half also used in pair 3). B donates its guarded-close ($close + 1e-8, 3 nodes); $earnings_per_share sits outside that division rather than dividing by it directly, because eps-over-guarded-close is B's own 5-node core and repeating it whole would trip archive_subtree against B. Fusion: dividing A's monthly liquidity peak by price reframes a dollar-concentration measure as a price-relative event-intensity measure, crossed with an earnings-level rank, an interaction neither parent has (A never sees a fundamental, B never normalizes anything by a liquidity peak). Flagged risk: this sits close in spirit to the already-live d514189e7f1b5496 (eps rank times a price-scaled dollar-volume-delta rank), so correlation is a real, unverified risk even though the transforms differ (level vs delta, cross-sectional rank vs 21-day time-series rank).

Positions today's dollar volume within its own 63-day high-low band (a liquidity stochastic): sitting near the floor means trading interest is drying up, implying a thinner book and wider effective spreads that should command a return premium, while sitting near the ceiling reflects a transient attention spike that tends to fade.

Crosses capital-efficiency quality with an acute, 5-day spike in a stock's own range percentile: a sharp volatility burst in a fundamentally efficient firm more likely reflects real news being digested by informed capital, whereas the identical burst in a low-quality firm is more likely noise trading with no follow-through.

Memory explicitly flags TS_DELTA($dollar_volume) as a weak cheap_screen performer (|t| 0.13-0.38), while level/TS_RANK forms drove most accepts, making the DELTA operator the clear weakest component. Swapped only that operator to TS_RANK, keeping the EPS leg, field and window unchanged.

Donated: A's TS_STD($book_per_share,63) (3 nodes) and B's TS_DELTA($volume,3) (3 nodes); A's other leg, $accrual_gap, is folded in as a bare field (not the 2-node CS_RANK($accrual_gap) A itself uses) to complete the earnings-quality story A only half-supplies elsewhere in this batch. A alone flags accrual/book-value risk with no trading-activity confirmation; B alone flags a raw volume shift with no fundamental-quality context. The three-way product surfaces names where accrual-flagged earnings quality, balance-sheet instability, AND a fresh shift in trading interest all point the same direction at once -- a compounded quality-meets-attention signal no single parent expresses.

Donated: A's TS_MEAN($roa,63) (3 nodes, the ROA half of A's ROE-minus-ROA spread, freed from A's own SUB/ZSCORE-of-the-whole-spread) and B's TS_DELTA($volume,3) (3 nodes). Each is standardized via CS_ZSCORE to avoid both parents' own wrappers and their scale mismatch. A alone is a static profitability level with no trading-activity content; B alone is a raw volume shift with no fundamental-quality context. The product reweights 'is trading interest picking up' by 'is this a fundamentally profitable business': a volume surge in a high-ROA name reads as informed accumulation, the same surge in a weak-ROA name reads as noise -- a conditioning neither parent expresses alone.
Return on assets earned per unit of leverage isolates capital-efficient profitability; ranking it against margin separates efficiency-driven returns from pricing-power-driven ones.

The accrual_gap leg is 2 nodes and safe untouched; the delta leg is exactly the 4-node CS_RANK(TS_DELTA(fundamental,63)) block memory flags as saturated regardless of field, and this parent's only child already swapped the operator (TS_DELTA->TS_STD, fitness fell to 2.96). Swapping the field instead keeps the endorsed 63-day delta window; leverage is unavailable here since CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($leverage,63)) is already a taken 4-node archive block, so asset_turnover is the untested option.

A donates $dollar_volume + 1e-8 (3 nodes). B donates TS_RANK($dollar_volume, 63) (3 nodes, its long-window liquidity leg). This is a weak cross: A's real idea, a close-position-in-range recovery signal, cannot be donated because its numerator ($close - $low) subtracts the dividend-adjusted close from the raw low, a lookahead-tainted scale mix by this repo's data convention, and A's own admission rationale already calls the window and denominator around it a known dead end. What remains is a generic dollar_volume guard that duplicates a guard pattern B already carries. The result, a quality-times-liquidity-rank product divided by raw dollar_volume, likely just tracks inverse liquidity level and probably collapses onto existing dollar_volume archive members. Reported as required, but this pair does not fuse cleanly.

This sits in the 'eps vs price level' niche flagged as fast-saturating (rule 7), and sibling 5da2da33 already covers the non-ABS variant against $close. Swap the saturating $close denominator to $book_per_share to move into a fresh fundamental-vs-fundamental ratio.

Persistent above-fast-baseline trading days mark a building accumulation/distribution phase rather than a one-day spike; sustained participation growth precedes continued price adjustment as more traders become aware of the name.

Both legs are scaled to each stock's own recent history before combining, so a high ratio means today's move is unusually large relative to how unusual today's volume is for that name: a thin-liquidity move achieved without much volume, which tends to partly revert.

Same numerator scale-mix issue as af43733e (this formula is c0a5abed's own admitted mutation of the same 9b349c02 parent). TS_STD($close,w) is already saturated at w=5/10/21/63 across archive and rejections, so kept the field but moved to an untested 126-day window alongside the $close->$open numerator fix, avoiding a verbatim restatement of the untouched denominator.

This lineage's sibling mutation (8f76527f, itself a child of this parent) documents that smoothing/shifting the $close denominator is a dead end here (TS_MEAN($close,5) was a within-run duplicate, TS_MEAN($close,21) hit rho 0.998) and that only a non-monotonic transform of EPS decorrelates. ABS(EPS) is already taken by 8f76527f and EPS/book_per_share variants are already archived, so used the complementary MIN(EPS,0) loss-floor (untested) instead of ABS's magnitude fold, targeting the same bare-EPS weak component with a distinct, non-monotonic lever.

This leg's own documented child (cf8910d8) states every OHLC-anchor swap tried on this exact ratio stayed at rho>=0.85, so an anchor swap alone will not clear correlation, and wrapping the untouched 7-node ratio in TS_RANK alone would restate it verbatim (archive_subtree). Combined an anchor change ($low->$high) with a TS_RANK(...,21) wrapper, converting the bare same-day ratio into a 21-day percentile -- the same kind of added temporal structure that cleared correlation elsewhere (rule 10's 3.713 accept) -- so the leg changes in kind, not just in which OHLC field it uses.

DELAY($close,1) is the most noise-sensitive component: a single stale print driving the whole ratio. Rejections show both smoothing it (TS_MEAN($close,5), rho 0.886) and a small shift bump (DELAY($close,5), rho 0.819) already fail just above the 0.80 threshold, with correlation dropping as the reference moves further from 'yesterday'. Pushed the shift substantially further to 21 to extend that same decorrelating trend rather than repeating an already-failed small tweak.

A donates TS_MAX($dollar_volume,21) (3 nodes, 21-day peak liquidity); B donates TS_DELTA($volume,3) (3 nodes, divided rather than RANKed so it doesn't recreate B's own RANK(TS_DELTA($volume,3))). B's short-horizon share-volume delta is rescaled by A's own recent dollar-liquidity ceiling, so a given volume change reads as a bigger surprise in a name whose typical liquidity is low than in a heavily-traded mega-cap; crossed with a fresh earnings rank. Neither parent normalizes a volume change by the stock's own liquidity scale. The share/dollar-volume unit mix is a deliberate scale adjustment (this codebase already mixes such units elsewhere, e.g. dcc42219621b8def), but correlation with sibling accrual_gap x volume-delta factors (98f5e83e9268cb7d and family) is unverified.

A donates TS_DELTA($volume,3) (3 nodes, under ABS so it doesn't recreate A's own RANK(TS_DELTA($volume,3))); B donates TS_MIN($low,21) (3 nodes, the 21-day floor). The floor is paired with the day's high rather than close to avoid restating B's own 5-node close-to-floor numerator, then TS_RANKed within the stock's own 63-day history (avoiding a cross-sectional raw-price-level scale mismatch) to measure how far today's high reaches above the recent floor; crossed with A's unsigned volume-shock magnitude. This asks whether a reach above the recent floor is volume-confirmed, which neither parent expresses alone: A never touches the price range, B has no volume or fundamental input.

A donates TS_MIN($low,21) (3 nodes, the 21-day price floor); B donates ($book_per_share + 1e-8) (3 nodes, its only legal fragment beyond the 2-node ABS(eps) leaf). The floor price is normalized by book value per share instead of B's own earnings numerator, producing a trough price-to-book ratio -- a margin-of-safety measure using the stock's recent low rather than its current price. Neither parent states this: A is a pure price oscillator with no fundamental, B never references price history.

Rising leverage over the past quarter combined with currently elevated income-inflating accruals compounds balance-sheet and earnings-quality risk at once; gating on an elevated dollar-volume percentile targets names where this deterioration is fresh news still being priced in rather than already stale.

Rule 9 flags <=5-day TS_DELTA on a bare OHLC field as return-equivalent and cheap-screen-failing; this parent's second leg is exactly that pattern. Lengthening the window past the flagged short-window zone is the direct fix.

A donates TS_RANK($dollar_volume, 63) and ($dollar_volume + 1e-8) (3 nodes each). B donates ($roe * $book_per_share) (3 nodes), wrapped in CS_ZSCORE rather than CS_RANK because CS_RANK canonicalizes to RANK and RANK($roe*$book_per_share) is exactly B's own archived branch. Fusion: grafts B's DuPont-style compounder measure (profitability earned on a real, larger equity base, not just a high rate on a tiny one) into A's liquidity-attention architecture in place of bare $roe -- asking whether the market is actively trading (relative to the stock's own baseline liquidity) substantial compounders specifically, not just any high-ROE name regardless of scale. A alone never distinguishes rate from scale; B alone never looks at liquidity. Risk flagged: this keeps A's entire skeleton, so it leans on the swapped quality measure alone to decorrelate -- roe*book_per_share is a materially different construct from bare roe (not just a same-dimension field swap), but this is the weakest-decorrelation candidate of the eight.

The open aggregates overnight order flow separately from the intraday auction that sets the close, so a stock opening near the top of both its 10-day and 63-day range reflects durable, multi-horizon-consistent overnight demand, a channel distinct from close-based momentum.

Keeps A's 63-day dollar-volume regime rank (3 nodes) and B's 21-day high (3 nodes), recombined as distance below the recent high rather than B's own close-minus-low-over-range measure. Captures whether a pullback from highs is happening in a high or low relative-volume regime. Neither parent has this: B carries no volume dimension, and A's other leg (ROE) cannot be donated at 3+ nodes without exceeding the shared-subtree limit.

Keeps A's daily range (3 nodes) and B's roe*book_per_share interaction (3 nodes), fused as quality-per-unit-of-volatility instead of either parent's own framing (a plain rank-product for A, a spread against leverage for B). The whole ratio is ranked once at the top, so neither bare fragment is directly RANK-wrapped the way B (and a third archive member built the same way) already wraps roe*book_per_share. Rewards quality that stands out relative to how much the name has been moving, a link neither parent expresses.

Range expansions that coincide with accelerating, not just elevated, turnover mark an intensifying information event rather than a stable high-volume regime, predicting stronger continuation than either signal alone.

Keeps TS_STD($close,21) from A, 3 nodes -- A's own ADD(TS_STD,eps) pairing is 5 nodes and the full DIV with SUB(close,low) is 9. Keeps ADD($close,1e-8) from B, 3 nodes -- B's other candidate donation, ABS($eps), is only 2 nodes, and pairing ABS(eps) directly over ADD(close,eps) the way B does would restate B's 6-node ratio whole, so ABS(eps) is re-ranked instead of divided by it. Fusion: earnings-magnitude rank scaled by (volatility / price), a coefficient-of-variation risk term -- large absolute earnings on a relatively volatile stock. B has no time-series/volatility information; A has no fundamental leg.

Keeps ADD($close,1e-8) from A, 3 nodes -- A's ABS($eps) alone is only 2 nodes, and pairing it over ADD(close,eps) as A does would restate A's 6-node ratio whole, so the numerator uses signed $eps instead. Keeps TS_MAX($high,21) from B, 3 nodes -- B's own SUB($close,TS_MAX(high,21)) is already 5 nodes, so $close is swapped for $low there to avoid restating B's exact pairing while keeping the 'distance from the recent high' shape. Fusion: how far today's LOW has fallen below the 21-day high, relative to price, signed by earnings rank -- a value-conditioned drawdown-from-high measure. A has no time-series information; B has no fundamental conditioning and isn't price-relative.

Keeps TS_STD($return,5) from B, 3 nodes -- B's full TS_CORR node is 6 nodes and would restate B whole if the window and second leg were left unchanged, so both are changed together (window 21->10, $volume -> TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63)). Keeps TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63) from A, 3 nodes -- pairing it back with A's CS_RANK(close-TS_MAX(high,21)) under the same MUL would restate A's 10-node whole, so that leg is dropped rather than forced in. Fusion: correlates short-horizon return volatility against the stock's OWN 63-day volume percentile rather than raw volume level -- a within-name-normalised version of B's contemporaneous vol-volume linkage. Honest limit: A's 'distance from the 21-day high' leg isn't used, only its volume-percentile leg, so the fusion is B's structure plus A's liquidity normaliser, not A's technical signal.

Earnings-quality risk is a threshold effect: only the most aggressive positive-accrual firms (income running ahead of cash flow) get downgraded, while every conservative-accrual firm ties at the top, sharpening the accrual anomaly with an asymmetric read.

Among firms not currently posting losses, price rising in lockstep with volume over the last two weeks signals informed accumulation confirming the quality thesis, favoring profitable names getting fresh conviction buying over those drifting on thin interest.

Requires firms to rank highly on both accumulated per-share capital base and current capital efficiency simultaneously, an AND-gate compounder signal that a single ratio or either field alone can't express.

The generic $close normalizer is the weakest component; per rule 5 this X is closed for several partners already. book_per_share is an untried denominator for the bare (non-ABS) ratio (only the ABS-wrapped version with book_per_share exists in the archive), giving eps a book-value scale instead of a price scale.

A normalizes its close-high reversal ratio by price level only and has no volume content. B's liquidity-rank leg only ever appears scaling a quality signal. This child conditions A's raw reversal pressure on B's liquidity-history percentile directly: does closing weak relative to the day's high matter more when the stock is currently trading heavy relative to its own recent volume history. That within-name liquidity confirmation is absent from both parents individually.

Drops both parents' fundamental and volume-correlation content to build a pure regime interaction: a stock's own liquidity-momentum percentile (A) times cross-sectionally high realized volatility (B), a joint vol-and-liquidity-spike detector. Caveat: a live archive member, b9168878094496ee, already correlates these same two atoms over a 10-day window. This child asks about simultaneous levels rather than time-series comovement, a different construct, but correlation risk against that neighbor, and against the pair-6 child below which reuses the same two atoms, is real and unverified without running the panel.

An accelerating rise in a high-ROA firm's percentile rank within its own 15-day range over just 3 days is more likely the market re-rating real earnings power than noise, so quality names breaking toward new local highs keep drifting up while the same move in low-ROA names tends to fade.

Lowest-fitness sibling of the same template. Memory warns that swapping only the normalizing field doesn't decorrelate, so the edit targets the numerator instead: close-vs-low becomes open-vs-low while $close stays as the normalizer.

A donates ($close - $high) (3 nodes, its numerator; A's own RANK(eps)-minus-RANK(...) top structure is dropped, that skeleton is saturated for any inner content per this lineage's own documented mutation history). B donates TS_MAX($high, 21) (3 nodes, its ceiling; B's own +1e-8 guarded denominator is dropped rather than reused, since guarding TS_MAX($high,21) with 1e-8 again would restate B's own 5-node denominator verbatim).
